articles.title: Nuveen Green Capital Closes $281M C-PACE Loan for Boston Condos
articles.narrative: Millennium Partners has secured a $281 million C-PACE loan for energy efficiency upgrades at the 62-story Winthrop Center in Downtown Boston. Nuveen Green Capital originated the fixed-rate loan, which represents the largest C-PACE financing in the New England region to date. This C-PACE debt closed concurrently with a $575 million CMBS loan for the office and retail components, forming a combined $856 million debt package that retires a previous construction loan.

data_points.notable_features: 62-story mixed-use building, one of Boston's tallest, located in the financial district.
data_points.project_notes: C-PACE loan secured under the PACE Massachusetts program. A $575 million CMBS loan was also secured for the office and retail portions. The combined debt package of $856 million takes out a prior construction loan from Cale Street originated in October 2020. The PACE Massachusetts program was updated in June 2026 by MassDevelopment and the Massachusetts Department of Energy Resources.

articles.title: Nalcorp, Clipper Equity Buy Coney Island Oceanfront Development Site for $20M
articles.narrative: Nalcorp and Clipper Equity have acquired an oceanfront development site in Coney Island, Brooklyn, for $20 million from Bath Site LLC. The 69,530-square-foot parcel, which includes 247 feet of Boardwalk frontage, is part of a larger development where permits were filed in 2024 for a 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building. This transaction represents a significant development deal in a rapidly transforming waterfront market, where opportunities for premier development sites are becoming increasingly scarce due to ongoing public and private investment.

data_points.address: 2015 Boardwalk West, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Oceanfront development site with 247 feet of Boardwalk frontage.
data_points.project_notes: Permits were filed in 2024 to build a 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building. The larger parcel was subdivided into six tax lots, with this specific lot (Block 7072, Lot 6) previously acquired by Bath Site LLC in July 2024 for $10.4 million.

articles.title: Survey: 61% of Investors Hold Negative Multifamily Outlook in 2026, Per Berkadia
articles.narrative: A recent survey by Berkadia indicates that 61% of real estate investors hold a negative outlook for the multifamily market in the second half of 2026, primarily due to persistent capital markets volatility. This sentiment contrasts with earlier optimism, as 52% of respondents reported worse-than-anticipated performance in the first half of the year. Despite this caution, investors are not losing confidence in multifamily as an asset class, with 82% planning portfolio expansion and 83% expecting market improvement by late 2027. The shift reflects a greater focus on execution risk, with investors scrutinizing rent growth assumptions, exit cap rates, and financing structures more closely, prioritizing core strategies over value-add opportunities. The Midwest region has emerged as a preferred investment destination, favored by 58% of investors for its durable cash flow potential and stronger rental growth assumptions compared to other regions.

articles.title: St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort Secures $263M Refi After Special Servicing
articles.narrative: Fortress Investment Group has provided a $263 million refinancing loan for the St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort, an oceanfront property in Bal Harbour, FL. The financing package, which includes $188 million in assumed existing debt and $70 million in new debt, rescued the 213-room resort from special servicing. The property, owned by Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company (ARTIC), was valued at $311 million in public mortgage documents.

data_points.notable_features: Oceanfront property with two pools, a 14,000-square-foot spa, five dining outposts, 13,000 square feet of event space, and a condo component.
data_points.project_notes: The property was previously acquired for $213 million in 2014. A $188 million CMBS loan tied to the resort went into special servicing in 2025 due to the lender's requirement for a replacement interest rate cap, despite the loan remaining current and the resort maintaining a debt service coverage ratio above break-even.

articles.title: First Pioneer Properties Buys Queens Retail Center for $24M
articles.narrative: First Pioneer Properties, in partnership with ABS Partners Real Estate, has acquired a 24,000-square-foot retail center in Bayside, Queens, from Levy Properties for $23.5 million. The one-story property, which includes significant air rights, currently houses an urgent care facility and a baby store. The buyers' plans for the site are not yet clear, but the acquisition comes amidst a wave of multifamily development activity in Queens.

data_points.notable_features: Includes 74,350 square feet of additional air rights for a total of 98,478 buildable square feet.

articles.title: Trademark Completes 321-Unit Vickery Apartments in Downtown Fort Worth

Developed in partnership with SCOA Real Estate Partners and designed by GFF, the project includes 307 apartments, 14 townhomes, and a 5,300-square-foot restaurant with a second-story lounge. Construction on the development began in February 2024 and was topped out in January 2025, with residential leasing commencing in fall 2025.

articles.title: Partnership Nears Completion of $158M Workforce Housing Project in Mount Vernon, New York
articles.narrative: A partnership between Simone Development Cos. and Stagg Group is nearing completion on Qwest Towers, a $158 million workforce housing project in Mount Vernon, New York. articles.title: SparrowHawk acquires EQT portfolio of 20 industrial assets across Midwest
articles.narrative: SparrowHawk, an industrial real estate investment and management firm, completed its largest transaction to date by acquiring a 20-property industrial portfolio totaling 4.4 million square feet across six Midwest logistics markets for just under $400 million. The acquisition from EQT expands SparrowHawk's presence in key regional growth markets including St. Louis, Cincinnati, Cleveland, Columbus, Dayton, and Louisville. The portfolio features a diverse tenant mix and is expected to provide significant rent growth opportunities, aligning with SparrowHawk's strategy for capital deployment and platform expansion.

data_points.notable_features: Portfolio located across six high-demand Midwest logistics markets: St. Louis, Cincinnati, Cleveland, Columbus, Dayton, and Louisville.

articles.title: MDH Partners acquires 1-million-square-foot industrial building in Greenfield
articles.narrative: MDH Partners has acquired 70 Connect III, a 1-million-square-foot Class A industrial building in Greenfield, Indiana, located within the Indianapolis metropolitan area. The speculative cross-docked facility, developed by Lauth, offers 40-foot clear heights and extensive dock and trailer parking. MDH plans immediate capital improvements to enhance the property for a large industrial user, including doubling trailer parking and expanding office space. The acquisition aligns with MDH's strategy of investing its $1.2 billion Fund III, having closed over $1 billion in assets since early 2025.

data_points.notable_features: Cross-docked building with 40-foot clear heights, 108 expandable to 216 dock doors, four drive-in doors, ESFR sprinkler system, and eight-inch slabs. Located less than three miles from Interstate 70.
data_points.project_notes: Developed by Lauth on a speculative basis. MDH plans to double trailer parking from 115 to approximately 230 positions, expand speculative office space, and complete interior/exterior repainting.

articles.market_intelligence: Indianapolis metro's overall industrial vacancy fell to 5.9% in Q2 2026, with 3.1 million square feet absorbed during the quarter and nearly 19 million square feet over the past 12 months. The East submarket, where 70 Connect III is located, saw vacancy drop from over 18% to 11% in the past year, remaining the highest vacancy rate in Indianapolis despite leading in leasing activity.

articles.title: Browning brings its Velocity formula to Columbus
articles.narrative: Browning, an Indianapolis-based developer, has broken ground on Velocity Hill Road, a 200,200-square-foot speculative industrial building in Canal Winchester, Ohio, marking its first ground-up development in the Columbus market. The project is part of Browning's Velocity industrial park brand and is strategically sized to meet demand for smaller industrial spaces, a niche identified by the developer in a market that has predominantly seen larger facility construction. The company undertook extensive research to ensure Columbus's logistics infrastructure, population growth, and manufacturing investment align with its development strategy, with the building expected to be completed by the end of 2026.

data_points.notable_features: Targeting LEED Silver certification, features 32-foot clear height, 10 dock doors, two drive-in doors, ESFR sprinklers, LED lighting, 2,000-amp electrical service, and parking for 200 vehicles. Located along the U.S. 33 corridor with quick highway access and walking distance to community amenities.
data_points.project_notes: Part of Browning's Velocity industrial park brand. The building can be divided into as many as four spaces, with additional land for trailer parking or outdoor storage.

articles.market_intelligence: Approximately 7.1 million square feet of speculative industrial space is under construction across the Columbus market, with an overall industrial vacancy rate of 5.6%. In the Southeast U.S. 33 Corridor, where Velocity Hill Road is located, there is no other speculative industrial product under construction and vacancy was 4.3%. Last year, the Columbus market recorded substantial absorption, including four 1-million-square-foot buildings being leased.

articles.title: After more than four decades in publishing, Mark Menzies retires from REjournals
articles.narrative: Mark Menzies, senior vice president and national publisher at REjournals, is retiring after more than four decades in the publishing industry. Menzies was instrumental in guiding REjournals through significant industry changes and economic shifts, including the 2008 recession, the transition to online publishing, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the emergence of AI. His career included 29 years with Law Bulletin Publishing before its real estate publications were acquired by REjournals, where he spent an additional seven years overseeing the growth of several key regional real estate journals.

articles.title: PMB, Loma Linda University Health Break Ground on Inpatient Rehab Hospital
